tasks.label: backend: free port 5236
tasks.detail: Free :5236 for the API launch configuration: SIGTERM the leftover listener (usually a `dotnet run` or debuggee orphaned to PPID 1 when a terminal closed), wait up to 6s, then SIGKILL — a hung host accepts TCP but never answers /health and ignores graceful shutdown, so SIGTERM alone is not enough.
tasks.command: pids=$(lsof -nP -iTCP:5236 -sTCP:LISTEN -t); if [ -z "$pids" ]; then echo ':5236 is already free'; else echo "freeing :5236 — SIGTERM to $pids"; kill -TERM $pids; for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do sleep 1; pids=$(lsof -nP -iTCP:5236 -sTCP:LISTEN -t); [ -z "$pids" ] && break; done; if [ -n "$pids" ]; then echo ":5236 still held by $pids after 6s (hung host ignores SIGTERM) — SIGKILL"; kill -9 $pids; sleep 2; pids=$(lsof -nP -iTCP:5236 -sTCP:LISTEN -t); fi; if [ -n "$pids" ]; then echo ":5236 is STILL held by $pids — stop the other debug session first"; exit 1; else echo ':5236 is free now'; fi; fi; curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 2 http://127.0.0.1:5236/health && echo ':5236 answers /health, something re-bound it' || echo ':5236 refuses connections — ready for F5'

tasks.label: frontend: free port 5173
tasks.detail: Free :5173 before the dev server (or the browser debugger) starts. vite.config.ts sets strictPort: true, so a leftover server is a hard failure — `Error: Port 5173 is already in use` — rather than a bump to 5174. The leftover is usually an `npm run dev` orphaned to PPID 1 when its terminal or debug session closed; it exits when its node child dies, so killing the listener is enough. SIGTERM, poll 6s, then SIGKILL, ending with a real HTTP probe.
tasks.command: pids=$(lsof -nP -iTCP:5173 -sTCP:LISTEN -t); if [ -z "$pids" ]; then echo ':5173 is already free'; else echo "freeing :5173 — SIGTERM to $pids"; kill -TERM $pids; for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do sleep 1; pids=$(lsof -nP -iTCP:5173 -sTCP:LISTEN -t); [ -z "$pids" ] && break; done; if [ -n "$pids" ]; then echo ":5173 still held by $pids after 6s — SIGKILL"; kill -9 $pids; sleep 2; pids=$(lsof -nP -iTCP:5173 -sTCP:LISTEN -t); fi; if [ -n "$pids" ]; then echo ":5173 is STILL held by $pids — stop the other dev server first"; exit 1; else echo ':5173 is free now'; fi; fi; curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 2 http://localhost:5173/ && echo ':5173 answers HTTP — something re-bound it' || echo ':5173 refuses connections — ready for the dev server'
